prompt: You are documenting an existing internal e-commerce system named `orderflow`. It has 4 services: `api-gateway` (Go), `order-service` (Python/FastAPI), `payment-service` (Python/FastAPI, owns Stripe integration), and `notification-service` (Node.js). They communicate via REST and a Kafka topic `order.events`. The team just decided to migrate from REST to gRPC for inter-service calls. Generate the architecture documentation set for this system, including the migration decision. Save every file you create into the CURRENT directory. Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions. Print the final list of files at the end.
assertions: At least one file uses Architecture Decision Record (ADR) format with the four canonical sections present as headings: 'Status', 'Context', 'Decision', AND 'Consequences' (case-insensitive, all four required in one file). A single architecture.md without these four named sections does NOT satisfy this.

The architecture documentation is split across THREE OR MORE distinct files (e.g., system-design.md, ownership-map.md, data-flow.md, adr-001-grpc.md, component-spec.md). A single monolithic architecture.md or a README + 1 file does NOT satisfy this.

At least one file contains an explicit per-service ownership or responsibility breakdown — either a table or a structured list mapping each of the 4 services (api-gateway, order-service, payment-service, notification-service) to its responsibility, owner, or scope. The mapping must enumerate ALL FOUR services individually (not just generic prose mentioning some of them).
